query: What lives in a Tough Tongue AI workspace? Name the resources, not just scenarios.
expected_behavior: Describes a workspace as a personal account or an organization

Names Scenarios, sessions, collections, FileBases, SIP trunks, bots (phone calls and meeting bots), the Scenario browser profile, access tokens, Knowledge Bases, Custom Functions, balance, and effective entitlements — not only Scenarios
Loads references/entities/resources.md (and account-and-access.md for balance/entitlements) rather than inventing the catalog
Points at references/mcp/tools.md when the user asks how to list or create those resources — does not dump an OAuth walkthrough unprompted

query: What can I do in our Tough Tongue AI organization workspace?
expected_behavior: Explains that it can work in an authorized organization workspace but cannot create organizations, administer members, change roles, or change plans
Names organization-scoped Scenarios, sessions, SIP calls, meeting bots, collections, safe resources, shared balance, and effective entitlements
Calls ttai:get_workspace_info before an organization-scoped tool when live tools are available and passes an opaque organizations[].id as org_id (never the slug)
Keeps orientation read-only unless the user explicitly requests a stateful action

query: Which fields do I set on a scenario besides the long AI instructions and the rubric?
expected_behavior: Loads references/scenario/model-selection.md and/or control.md and does not paste a full ai_instructions essay

Covers ai_model_config (realtime Galaxy/Ocean, Landmass realtime with separate TTS, Landmass cascade; cold call and slide demos start on Landmass cascade + Cartesia, sales roleplay on Galaxy, coaching and browser demos on Ocean; super Scenarios require Landmass; never cascade-01; never invent tts_voice_id)

Covers strategy (opening lives in FLOW, no welcome_instructions field; omitted silence means 120 s then hang up), appearance.voice and language_code, an explicit tools_config with end_session, and session_analysis.is_auto_analysis
Points at references/scenario/ai-instructions.md for the instruction shape and a recipe under references/recipes/ for rubric patterns

query: How should ai_instructions be structured? Don't write a cold-call script — just the skeleton.
expected_behavior: Loads references/scenario/ai-instructions.md and gives the fundamental sections (CONTEXT, ROLE, FLOW, TOOLS, GUARDRAILS, STYLE) without a situation-specific opening
States one question per turn, a directive FLOW opening (no welcome_instructions field), and that every {{ var }} needs a missing-value fallback
Mentions recipes exist for cold call, sales roleplay, coaching, demo, interview, and meeting facilitation rather than inlining one
Gives at most a one-line pointer to create/update tools — no OAuth walkthrough

query: Call ttai:get_workspace_info and show me the result.
expected_behavior: Calls ttai:get_workspace_info (or explains how to connect if tools are missing)
On success, reports the personal workspace and organizations by name with the caller's role
Does not author Scenario field tables in the same turn

query: I just installed the plugin but I'm getting 401 errors from ttai tools.
expected_behavior: Treats 401 as OAuth not completed for this client (Claude Code /mcp, Codex mcp login ttai, Cursor Settings > MCP) using references/mcp/clients.md
Never asks the user to paste a token or other credential into chat
For CI, server, or webhook setups, links the public headless setup page and writes no credential setup itself
For Claude Code over SSH with no local browser, suggests claude mcp login plugin:toughtongue:ttai --no-browser in an interactive terminal (ssh -t), and does not offer it for CI or claude -p

query: I just connected Tough Tongue AI. What can I do here?
expected_behavior: Calls ttai:read_guide before broad account inventory when it is available, otherwise reports the guide/catalog rollout mismatch
Verifies with ttai:get_workspace_info and takes a light inventory with small typed lists
Keeps orientation read-only and does not create, update, call, schedule, or share anything

query: How do I update an existing scenario versus creating a new one?
expected_behavior: ttai:create_scenario rejects id and requires name + ai_instructions; ttai:update_scenario requires id and changes only the fields sent
Explains merge rules: nested objects like strategy merge one level, but a tool's tool_settings and the whole ai_model_config are replaced — read, merge, and write the full object
Says to load the live tool schema first and notes edits apply to new sessions only
Points at references/scenario/workflow.md and references/mcp/tools.md

query: I am building a web chat companion. What context should I give it before it recommends or changes a Tough Tongue AI scenario?
expected_behavior: Describes the operating model as provider-neutral rather than tied to a CLI or a second API client
Requests or reuses verified workspace scope, focused Scenario/resource, user intent, consumer capabilities, and any live account facts (the optional context packet)
Distinguishes platform support, consumer tool availability, user entitlement, and the user's explicit request
Says the web companion must not assume a terminal or call a write action merely because it can recommend one

query: What plan am I on, and can I make SIP calls?
expected_behavior: Uses ttai:get_workspace_info (sections plan) as the caller's effective capability source when available, otherwise reports that the deployed catalog lacks it
Does not infer a plan from balance or from a Scenario
May use ttai:get_workspace_info (sections balance) for available minutes when relevant
Treats the live server response as authoritative for SIP access rather than guessing a tier, and lists SIP trunks before suggesting a call

query: For a cold-call scenario, should the AI end the session as soon as it says goodbye?
expected_behavior: Explains the response-gated close: state the outcome and goodbye first, then call end_session only after the other person's reply
Says end_session must not share a turn with a pitch, question, summary, or goodbye
Distinguishes ordinary thanks, noise, and crosstalk from substantive re-engagement; the latter cancels a pending end (endSession with cancel) before responding
Points to references/scenario/authoring.md or the cold-call recipe instead of inventing runtime behavior

query: Create a Tough Tongue AI scenario for my SDRs to practice cold-calling leads who filled out a demo form for our payroll software. The AI should play the caller.
expected_behavior: Calls ttai:read_guide first when available and the guide is not already in context, then resolves whether to pass an org_id with ttai:get_workspace_info (organizations)
Follows references/scenario/workflow.md: loads the cold-call recipe plus authoring, model-selection, control, and ai-instructions references

Drafts from supplied lead facts with a two-beat directive opening and the recipe's three outcomes (CONVERTED / NURTURE / DEAD LEAD); prefers Landmass cascade and uses Ocean only when Cascade/Cartesia is unavailable; never invents a TTS voice ID
Writes a rubric that evaluates the LEAD (the human), not the AI caller, and sends an explicit tools_config with end_session
Calls ttai:create_scenario without an id field and returns the practice link https://app.toughtongueai.com/run/<scenario_id>

query: Here is a transcript of a call we lost on pricing objections: [transcript]. Build me a practice scenario so our reps can rehearse handling these exact objections.
expected_behavior: Classifies the scenario as sales roleplay (AI plays the prospect) and loads references/recipes/sales-roleplay.md
Extracts the actual objections from the pasted transcript and uses them as the core objections instead of inventing generic ones
Includes a resistance pattern (one objection at a time), breakthrough conditions, and early termination rules in ai_instructions
Writes a rubric that evaluates the SALES REP with weighted categories
Creates via ttai:create_scenario and reports what was built in 2-3 sentences with the practice link

query: Our onboarding scenario keeps ending calls before the goodbye. Scenario name is 'Customer Onboarding Walkthrough'. Find out why and fix it.
expected_behavior: Uses a current Scenario ID when available; otherwise resolves the title with one ttai:list_resources(scenarios, query: <title>) call, then fetches full current detail with ttai:get_resource(scenarios)
Pulls compact session evidence via ttai:list_resources(sessions) filtered by scenario_ids, then inspects selected transcripts before proposing any edit
Loads references/scenario/runtime.md, diagnoses one root cause from the evidence, and distinguishes the prescribed behavior from what happened
Applies a surgical edit via ttai:update_scenario sending only id plus the changed fields (full tool_settings if a tool's settings change)
Reports diagnosis, change summary, and the new-sessions-only reminder

query: I attached two PDFs with our product FAQ. Make my scenario answer from them.
expected_behavior: Distills the attached PDFs into focused markdown files plus a root index.md (what is inside, links to every other file; under ~4 KB), not README.md
Calls ttai:create_filebase(kind: knowledge) then ttai:write_filebase with index.md first; does not use legacy knowledge-bases or knowledge_base_ids
Keeps any knowledge_filebase_ids already linked (the list is replaced whole and reads omit it), or tells the user linking replaces them and gets a go-ahead
Links the FileBase id via knowledge_filebase_ids on ttai:update_scenario after confirming with the user
Explains the agent gets getKnowledgeBite(filepath, start?, lines?) as <base name>/<path> and listKnowledgeBites(base), and that anyone who can run the scenario can have the agent read the base

query: Create a practice scenario where my reps cold-call a small-business owner who filled out a form last month. The AI plays the owner.
expected_behavior: Classifies the scenario as sales roleplay (the human is the caller) and loads references/recipes/sales-roleplay.md, not the cold-call recipe
Gives the prospect one bare first line ("Hello, who is this?") marked word for word, with no self-introduction, reason for the call, or permission ask; keeps skip_auto_start true
Sets force_agent_to_speak false so the silence nudge stays in character, and adds a pitch-reception phase (two or three how-does-it-work questions) before the first objection
Leaves no unlabelled quoted dialogue in ai_instructions: example phrases are plain text marked tone only, and only word-for-word lines are quoted
Writes a rubric that evaluates the REP and calls ttai:create_scenario with an explicit tools_config including end_session

query: Our cold-call agent sounds robotic and says the same 'Totally get it' line on every call. Scenario name is 'Payroll Demo Follow-up'. Fix it.
expected_behavior: Resolves the Scenario by title with one ttai:list_resources(scenarios, query) call, then fetches it with ttai:get_resource(scenarios)
Diagnoses unlabelled quoted lines in ai_instructions as the cause, per references/scenario/ai-instructions.md (Spoken lines) and runtime.md

Strips the quotation marks and code fences from the branch and objection lines, keeps the wording and marks it tone only, and adds the anti-robotic STYLE rule (never repeat the same sentence; one varied-acknowledgment example, not a paragraph)
Does not add a paragraph of sample lines or switch system_instructions_template as a side effect
Applies a surgical ttai:update_scenario with id plus ai_instructions only, and reminds that edits affect new sessions only

query: I want one scenario that can play either a trusting first-time buyer or a researched sceptic, chosen when the rep starts the run.
expected_behavior: Loads references/scenario/dynamic-variables.md and proposes one Scenario with a {% case level %} block on a variable (with a default), not two Scenarios
Explains how the value arrives: ?t_level= on the run link or dynamic_vars on calls and bots, and that the web run page asks for any referenced variable that is missing
States the two Liquid limits: values arrive as strings (convert with plus: 0 before a numeric comparison) and any Liquid error falls the text back to the raw template
Keeps the persona differences in character detail and resistance, with no unlabelled quoted dialogue
Creates via ttai:create_scenario and returns run links for both variants

query: My slide-based coaching scenario pops up the MCQ while the coach is still explaining the slide. Scenario name is 'Pricing Coach'. Fix it.
expected_behavior: Reads the live Scenario with ttai:get_resource before editing, because update_scenario replaces ai_instructions whole
Loads references/recipes/coaching.md and applies Mandatory Rules 3–4

Rewrites every FLOW step that runs an MCQ so the explanation ends with a check-in written as a plain directive in the step (ask if they have any questions or are ready for a quick check, and wait; answer any question; then run the MCQ), not a quoted line and not only a general rule
Has the MCQ shown with the mcq tool before the question is read aloud
Changes nothing else in the prompt and saves through ttai:update_scenario

query: Build a coaching scenario that teaches new support agents our three-step refund policy, one step per card, with a quick MCQ after each step.
expected_behavior: Loads references/recipes/coaching.md and uses Pattern B (Teach-First)
Each card step ends with a check-in written as a plain directive and a wait, and the MCQ runs only after the reply
States that the MCQ is shown with the mcq tool first and the question is read only once it is on screen
Sends an explicit tools_config with card, mcq and end_session, on Ocean medium-stable
Creates via ttai:create_scenario

query: Trainees say my coaching scenario marks them wrong when they explain the idea in their own words, and once when the transcript was garbled. Scenario name is 'Refund Policy Coach'. Fix it.
expected_behavior: Reads the live Scenario with ttai:get_resource before editing, because update_scenario replaces ai_instructions whole

Loads references/recipes/coaching.md (Judging Spoken Answers) and adds the judging routine to the prompt once: judge the CORE IDEA by meaning, be lenient on close variations, one more try in their own words, never a word-for-word repeat
Gives each spoken check a CORE IDEA, passing and not-passing examples, and asks for a repeat when the words look garbled or cut off
Keeps must-be-exact items exact (refund window, amounts) and names them
Updates the rubric to judge meaning too, and saves through ttai:update_scenario without changing anything else

query: Use slides instead of cards in my 'Objection Basics Coach' scenario. Here's the deck: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/e/EXAMPLE/pub
expected_behavior: Loads references/scenario/control.md (Google Slides decks) and reads the live Scenario with ttai:get_resource before editing
Sets google_slides tool_settings.embedUrl to the /pubembed form of the link, and turns card, image_generation and slide_generation off
Builds the SLIDE MAP from the deck's real text, or asks the user for it when the deck cannot be opened; never guesses slide content
Writes a SLIDE MAP with the exact slide count and one line per slide (key figures included), and starts each FLOW step with its slide
Keeps the curriculum, mentions the deck in user_instructions, updates via ttai:update_scenario with a save_as_version label for the new version, then re-fetches to verify
